components.name: ActivityBar
components.description:
The narrow vertical icon rail at the edge of the shell, used to switch which
panel the adjacent {@link SidebarPane} shows.

Controlled — it holds no selection state. `side` docks it left or right; for
the store-backed variants used by `ShellLayout`, see `ConnectedActivityBar`
and `ConnectedInspectorBar`.
components.example:
<ActivityBar
  items={[{ id: 'files', label: 'Explorer', icon: Files }]}
  activeId={active}
  onSelect={(id) => setActive(id === active ? null : id)}
/>

props.name: activeId
props.description: Id of the currently active item, or `null` when nothing is selected.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible label for the landmark. Defaults to `"Activity Bar"`.

props.name: bottomItems
props.description:
Items rendered in the bottom group, below the flex spacer. Defaults to a
single Settings item. Pass `[]` to render no bottom group.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes merged onto the root `<aside>`.

props.name: items
props.description: Items rendered in the main (top) group, in order.

props.name: onSelect
props.description:
Called with the clicked item's id. Toggling — clicking the active item to
deselect it — is the caller's decision, not the component's.

props.name: side
props.description:
Which edge of the shell the rail is docked to. Defaults to `"left"`.

The divider and the active-item indicator both mirror, so a right-hand rail
marks its selection on the edge facing the content.

components.name: AppTitle
components.description:
A branding lockup — icon badge, title and subtitle — sized for the
{@link MenuBar}'s `title` slot.

Purely presentational. Pass whatever branding your app needs; the library
supplies no default copy.
components.example:
<MenuBar
  title={<AppTitle title="Acme Studio" subtitle="Design System" icon={<Boxes size={16} />} />}
/>

props.name: title
props.description: Primary line. Rendered uppercase in a mono face.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes merged onto the root element.

props.name: icon
props.description:
Element shown in the leading badge, typically a 16px `lucide-react` icon.
Omit to render no badge at all.

props.name: subtitle
props.description: Secondary line beneath the title. Omit to render a single line.

components.name: ChatPane
components.description:
A chat panel: a scrolling transcript over a composer with slash-command
autocomplete.

Fully controlled — it owns only the in-progress input and the suggestion
highlight. Messages, sending and visibility belong to the caller, so the same
component works against a local array, a websocket, or an LLM endpoint. For
the store-backed variant, see `ConnectedChatPane`.

**It fills whatever hosts it.** Register it as a sidebar panel, an inspector
panel or a dockable tab and it takes that shape; it carries no width or edge
of its own. Inside a host that draws a title bar it omits its own header —
see `chrome` to override.
components.example:
<ChatPane
  messages={messages}
  onSend={(text) => send(text)}
  slashCommands={[{ command: 'clear', description: 'Clear the transcript' }]}
  onClose={() => setOpen(false)}
/>

props.name: chrome
props.description:
Draw the title bar.

Left unset, this follows the host: inside a `SidebarPane` or a dockable tab
the title is already drawn, so the pane omits its own. Set it explicitly to
force either way — which is also what lets the component be tested without
a host around it.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes merged onto the root element.

props.name: emptyState
props.description: Shown in place of the transcript when `messages` is empty.

props.name: messages
props.description: Messages to display, oldest first.

props.name: onClose
props.description: Called when the close button is pressed. Omit to hide the button.

props.name: onSend
props.description:
Called with the trimmed message text on send. The component clears its
composer but does not append to `messages` — that is the caller's job.

props.name: onSlashCommand
props.description: Called when a slash command is picked from the suggestion list.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder for the composer.

props.name: slashCommands
props.description: Slash commands offered once the composer starts with `/`.

props.name: title
props.description: Title shown in the pane header. Defaults to `"Chat"`.

components.name: CheckboxField
components.description:
A boolean property.

When `mixed`, the box renders indeterminate — neither on nor off — which is
the only honest state for a selection that disagrees.

components.name: ColorField
components.description: A colour property, as a swatch plus an editable hex value.

props.name: label
props.description: Label shown above the control.

props.name: value
props.description: Current value. `undefined` renders as empty.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes merged onto the field wrapper.

props.name: description
props.description: One line under the label explaining the property.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Render read-only.

props.name: error
props.description: Validation message, shown in the destructive colour.

props.name: mixed
props.description:
Selected subjects hold different values. The control shows a placeholder
instead of a value, and editing applies to all of them.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the new value.

props.name: showValue
props.description: Show the hex value in an editable text box beside the swatch. Default `true`.

components.name: CommandPalette
components.description:
A VS Code-style command palette: a fuzzy-filtered, keyboard-navigable list of
commands over a dimmed backdrop.

Fully controlled — it owns only the query text and the highlighted row.
Visibility, the command list and execution are the caller's. It also binds no
global keyboard shortcut; for the store-backed variant that reads the
{@link commandRegistry} and binds `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+P`, see
`ConnectedCommandPalette`.

Arrow keys move the highlight, Enter selects, Escape closes.
components.example:
<CommandPalette
  open={open}
  commands={[{ id: 'file.save', label: 'Save File', keybinding: '⌘S' }]}
  onSelect={(cmd) => { run(cmd.id); setOpen(false); }}
  onClose={() => setOpen(false)}
/>

props.name: commands
props.description: Commands to offer. Filtered against the query by `label` and `id`.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Called with the chosen command on click or Enter.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the palette is showing.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes merged onto the palette surface.

props.name: filter
props.description:
Custom filter. Receives every command and the current query; return `true`
to keep. Defaults to a case-insensitive substring match on `label` and `id`.

props.name: inline
props.description:
Render inline instead of as a fixed overlay. Useful for documenting the
palette in Storybook, or embedding it in a page. Defaults to `false`.

props.name: onClose
props.description: Called on Escape and on backdrop click.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder for the query input.

components.name: ContextMenu
components.description:
A floating menu positioned at viewport coordinates, for right-click menus.

Renders `position: fixed` at the given point and closes on outside click or
Escape. It does not decide when to appear — mount it conditionally from your
own `onContextMenu` handler and store the coordinates yourself.

props.name: items
props.description: Entries to show, in order.

props.name: onClose
props.description: Called on outside click, on Escape, and after any entry is chosen.

props.name: x
props.description: Viewport x coordinate, typically `event.clientX`.

props.name: y
props.description: Viewport y coordinate, typically `event.clientY`.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes merged onto the menu surface.

components.name: DataGrid
components.description:
A sortable, filterable data table with optional row virtualisation.

Filtering and sorting are handled internally against the `data` you pass — a
case-insensitive match across all values, and click-to-sort on columns marked
`sortable`. For server-side paging or sorting, filter upstream and set
`showFilter={false}`.
components.example:
<DataGrid
  columns={[
    { key: 'name', header: 'Name', sortable: true },
    { key: 'status', header: 'Status', width: 120,
      render: (v) => <Badge>{v}</Badge> },
  ]}
  data={rows}
  onRowClick={(row) => select(row.id)}
/>

props.name: columns
props.description: Columns, in display order.

props.name: data
props.description: Rows to display. Sorting and filtering are applied on top of this array.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes merged onto the root element.

props.name: loading
props.description: Show a loading indicator in place of rows. Defaults to `false`.

props.name: onRowClick
props.description: Called with the clicked row.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Message shown when there are no rows.

props.name: rowKey
props.description: Property used as each row's identity. Defaults to `"id"`.

props.name: selectedRowId
props.description: Value of `rowKey` on the row to highlight as selected.

props.name: showFilter
props.description: Show the built-in filter box above the grid. Defaults to `true`.

props.name: virtualized
props.description:
Virtualise rows with `react-virtuoso`. Leave on for large datasets; turn it
off when the grid must print or be fully present in the DOM. Defaults to
`true`.

components.name: DateField
components.description:
A date property, as an ISO `yyyy-mm-dd` string (or `yyyy-mm-ddThh:mm` with
`withTime`). A string rather than a `Date` so it round-trips through JSON
unchanged.

props.name: label
props.description: Label shown above the control.

props.name: value
props.description: Current value. `undefined` renders as empty.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes merged onto the field wrapper.

props.name: description
props.description: One line under the label explaining the property.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Render read-only.

props.name: error
props.description: Validation message, shown in the destructive colour.

props.name: max
props.description: Latest selectable date, in the same ISO form as `value`.

props.name: min
props.description: Earliest selectable date, in the same ISO form as `value`.

props.name: mixed
props.description:
Selected subjects hold different values. The control shows a placeholder
instead of a value, and editing applies to all of them.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the new value.

props.name: withTime
props.description: Include a time component. Defaults to `false`.

components.name: FieldShell
components.description:
The label, description and error frame shared by every property field.

Exported so a bespoke field looks like the built-in ones without copying
their markup — which is exactly what went wrong in the examples this family
replaces, where the same label styling was pasted into three inspectors.
components.example:
<FieldShell label="Opacity" description="0 to 1" htmlFor="opacity">
  <MyCustomSlider id="opacity" />
</FieldShell>

props.name: children
props.description: The control itself.

props.name: label
props.description: Label shown above the control, or beside it when `inline`.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes merged onto the field wrapper.

props.name: description
props.description: One line under the control explaining the property. Hidden while `error` is set.

props.name: error
props.description: Validation message, shown in the destructive colour in place of the description.

props.name: htmlFor
props.description: Associates the label with the control.

props.name: inline
props.description:
Render the label beside the control rather than above. Suits checkboxes,
where a label on its own line reads as a heading for nothing.

props.name: mixed
props.description: Selected subjects hold different values — renders the *Mixed* marker beside the label.

components.name: GraphCanvas
components.description:
An infinite, pannable, zoomable field to draw a graph on.

The canvas owns exactly one thing: the mapping between screen pixels and
graph space. It knows nothing about nodes, edges, or what any of it means —
children are rendered inside a transformed layer, so anything positioned in
graph coordinates lands in the right place.

Pan by dragging empty space or with the middle mouse button; zoom with the
wheel or a trackpad pinch, always anchored to the cursor. Space-drag pans
from anywhere, including over a node.

Viewport state is internal by default. Pass `viewport` to take control.
components.example:
<GraphCanvas onDrop={(point) => addNodeAt(point)}>
  {nodes.map((node) => (
    <GraphNode key={node.id} node={node} onMove={move}>
      {node.label}
    </GraphNode>
  ))}
</GraphCanvas>

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible label for the canvas region. Defaults to `"Graph canvas"`.

props.name: children
props.description:
Content rendered in graph space. Position children with `GraphNode`, or
with your own absolutely-positioned elements in graph coordinates.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes merged onto the root element.

props.name: defaultViewport
props.description: Starting viewport when uncontrolled. Defaults to origin at 1× zoom.

props.name: grid
props.description: Show the dot grid. Defaults to `true`.

props.name: gridSize
props.description: Grid spacing in graph units. Defaults to `24`.

props.name: maxScale
props.description: Largest allowed zoom. Defaults to `4`.

props.name: minScale
props.description: Smallest allowed zoom. Defaults to `0.1`.

props.name: onCanvasClick
props.description:
Called with a graph-space point when empty canvas is clicked. Use it to
clear selection, or to place a node at the click.

props.name: onCanvasContextMenu
props.description: Called with a graph-space point on right-click of empty canvas.

props.name: onCanvasDoubleClick
props.description: Called with a graph-space point when empty canvas is double-clicked.

props.name: onDrop
props.description:
Called when something is dropped on the canvas, with the graph-space point
under the cursor. Pair with `NodePalette` for drag-to-create.

props.name: onSizeChange
props.description:
Called on mount and whenever the element resizes, with its pixel size.

Pass this to a {@link GraphMiniMap} as `canvasSize` — the indicator cannot
be drawn without knowing how much of the graph is on screen.

props.name: onViewportChange
props.description: Called whenever pan or zoom changes, controlled or not.

props.name: overlay
props.description:
Content rendered in screen space, above the graph and unaffected by pan or
zoom — toolbars, a minimap, a legend.

props.name: pannable
props.description: Allow panning by dragging empty canvas. Defaults to `true`.

props.name: viewport
props.description:
Take control of pan and zoom. Omit it and the canvas manages its own,
which is what most callers want: you should not have to own a viewport
just to draw a graph.

props.name: zoomable
props.description: Allow zooming with the wheel or trackpad pinch. Defaults to `true`.

components.name: GraphEdge
components.description:
A directed edge between two nodes, rendered as an SVG path.

Which sides the edge leaves and enters is worked out from the nodes'
relative positions, so a node needs no handle configuration to be
connectable — move a node and the attachment points follow.

Render inside {@link GraphEdgeLayer}, which provides the SVG surface and the
arrowhead marker.
components.example:
<GraphEdgeLayer>
  {edges.map((edge) => (
    <GraphEdge
      key={edge.id}
      edge={edge}
      source={byId[edge.source]}
      target={byId[edge.target]}
      onSelect={setSelectedEdge}
    />
  ))}
</GraphEdgeLayer>

props.name: edge
props.description: The edge to render.

props.name: source
props.description: The node the edge leaves.

props.name: target
props.description: The node the edge enters.

props.name: arrow
props.description: Draw an arrowhead at the target end. Defaults to `true`.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes merged onto the visible path.

props.name: onContextMenu
props.type: (id: string, point: IPoint, event: React.MouseEvent) => void
props.description: Called on right-click, with the client point for a context menu.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Called on click. The wide invisible hit area makes this practical.

props.name: routing
props.description: Path shape. Defaults to `"bezier"`.

props.name: selected
props.description: Draw as selected.

components.name: GraphEdgeLayer
components.description:
The SVG surface edges are drawn on.

Sits beneath the nodes inside a {@link GraphCanvas}, spanning an effectively
unbounded area so edges remain visible wherever the graph is panned. It also
defines the shared arrowhead marker.

props.name: children
props.description: The edges to draw. Anything SVG works — this is just the surface.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes merged onto the `<svg>` element.

components.name: GraphMiniMap
components.description:
A scaled overview of the whole graph, with an indicator showing what the
canvas is currently looking at.

Click anywhere to jump there, drag to pan continuously, or focus it and use
the arrow keys. The zoom level is never changed — a minimap answers "where am
I", and changing scale on a click makes that answer harder to trust.

The plotted extent is the union of the graph's bounds and the current
viewport, so the indicator stays visible even when you have panned far away
from every node. Without that, panning into empty space makes the minimap
appear broken.

Fully controlled: it reads `viewport` and reports where you want to go, but
never moves the canvas itself.

props.name: canvasSize
props.description:
Pixel size of the canvas the minimap mirrors. Get it from `GraphCanvas`'s
`onSizeChange`; without it the viewport indicator can't be drawn.

props.name: nodes
props.description: The nodes to plot. Only position and size are read.

props.name: viewport
props.description: The canvas's current pan and zoom.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible label. Defaults to `"Graph minimap"`.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes merged onto the root element.

props.name: height
props.description: Minimap height in pixels. Defaults to `120`.

props.name: highlightIds
props.description:
Highlight these node ids — a selection, or search results. Drawn in the
primary colour above the rest.

props.name: nodeColor
props.description:
Fill colour for a node, as a CSS colour or Tailwind class. Receives the
node, so you can colour by `kind`. Defaults to the muted foreground.

props.name: onViewportChange
props.description:
Called with a viewport that recentres the canvas. Omit it and the minimap
becomes a read-only overview.

props.name: padding
props.description: Padding around the plotted content, in minimap pixels. Defaults to `8`.

props.name: panDistance
props.description: How far an arrow key pans, in graph units. Defaults to `80`.

props.name: width
props.description: Minimap width in pixels. Defaults to `180`.

components.name: GraphNode
components.description:
A positioned, focusable node on a {@link GraphCanvas}.

Provides placement, dragging, selection and focus affordances, and the four
edge ports. What the node *contains* is entirely yours — pass any children.

Fully controlled: dragging reports positions through `onMove` but never moves
the node itself, so snapping, constraints and undo stay in your hands.
components.example:
setNodes(move(nodes, id, position))} onActivate={(id) => setEditing(id)} >

{node.data.label}

props.name: node
props.description: The node to render. Position and size come from here.

props.name: children
props.description: Node body. Anything — a label, a form, a chart.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes merged onto the node element.

props.name: draggable
props.description: Allow dragging. Defaults to `true`.

props.name: focused
props.description:
Draw as focused — the keyboard cursor. Distinct from `selected`: focus is
where the next keystroke lands, selection is what an action applies to.

props.name: onActivate
props.description: Called on double-click. Conventionally enters edit mode.

props.name: onConnectEnd
props.description:
Called when a pointer is released over this node, with its id — the target
end of a connection started elsewhere.

props.name: onConnectStart
props.description:
Called when one of the node's ports is dragged, to begin a connection.
Providing it is what makes the ports appear.

props.name: onContextMenu
props.type: (id: string, point: IPoint, event: React.MouseEvent) => void
props.description: Called on right-click, with the client point for a context menu.

props.name: onMove
props.description:
Called with the new top-left position while dragging, and again on
release. The component never mutates the node — you apply the move, which
is what lets you snap, constrain or reject it.

props.name: onMoveEnd
props.description: Called when the drag ends, if the node actually moved.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Called on click.

props.name: ports
props.description: Show connection ports on hover and while focused. Defaults to `true`.

props.name: selected
props.description: Draw as selected.

components.name: MenuBar
components.description:
The application menu bar: a row of hover-activated dropdowns with optional
one-level submenus, plus slots for branding, a centre widget and right-hand
actions.

Presentational and fully controlled — menus come in as data and selections go
out through `onSelect`. It reads no registry. For the variant wired to the
{@link menuRegistry} and {@link commandRegistry}, see `ConnectedMenuBar`.
components.example:
<MenuBar
  menus={{ File: [{ id: 'save', label: 'Save', keybinding: '⌘S' }] }}
  onSelect={(item) => run(item.id)}
  right={<ThemeSwitcher value={theme} onChange={setTheme} />}
/>

props.name: center
props.description:
Slot between the menus and the right edge, sized for a search input. The
bar renders whatever you pass — it does not embed a search component.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes merged onto the root `<header>`.

props.name: menus
props.description:
Menus keyed by top-level label, e.g. `{ File: [...], Edit: [...] }`.
Insertion order determines display order.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Called with the chosen leaf item. Items with a `submenu` never fire this.

props.name: right
props.description: Slot at the far right, for a theme switcher, avatar, or actions.

props.name: title
props.description:
Branding shown at the far left. Pass a string, a logo element, or omit it
for the default wordmark. Providing a `title` switches the bar to its
taller, translucent variant.

components.name: Modal
components.description:
A centered modal dialog covering the three common blocking interactions:
alert, confirm and prompt.

Fully controlled — it owns only the prompt's draft text. Escape, backdrop
click and the close button all route to `onCancel`; Enter routes to
`onConfirm`. For the promise-based variant driven by `useModalStore` (so you
can `await openConfirm(...)` from anywhere), see `ConnectedModal`.
components.example:
<Modal
  open={open}
  type="prompt"
  title="Rename file"
  message="Enter a new name."
  defaultValue="untitled.ts"
  onConfirm={(name) => rename(name)}
  onCancel={() => setOpen(false)}
/>

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the dialog is mounted. Nothing renders when `false`.

props.name: title
props.description: Heading text.

props.name: cancelLabel
props.description: Label for the cancel button. Defaults to `"Cancel"`.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes merged onto the dialog surface.

props.name: confirmLabel
props.description: Label for the confirm button. Defaults to `"OK"` / `"Confirm"` by `type`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Initial value of the input when `type` is `"prompt"`.

props.name: message
props.description: Body text. Newlines are preserved.

props.name: onCancel
props.description: Called on Cancel, on the close button, on Escape, and on backdrop click.

props.name: onConfirm
props.description:
Called on Confirm/OK and on Enter. Receives the input text for `prompt`,
and `undefined` for `alert` and `confirm`.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder for the prompt input.

props.name: type
props.description: Dialog shape. Defaults to `"alert"`.

components.name: NodePalette
components.description:
A palette of node types that can be dragged onto a {@link GraphCanvas}, or
activated with the keyboard.

The palette carries only the item's `kind` on the drag; what a node of that
kind actually *is* is decided by your drop handler. Pair it with
{@link readPaletteDrag} on the canvas.

Every item is a real button, so the palette is fully usable without a
pointer — `onSelect` fires on click or Enter.

## Orientation

`auto` (the default) measures the space the palette's container gives it and
picks the axis that fits:

1. a row, if the items fit the available width;
2. otherwise a column, if they fit the available height;
3. otherwise a row that wraps.

A container that shrink-wraps its content — an absolutely positioned overlay,
say — offers no information about available space, so the palette measures
the nearest ancestor that has a size of its own. That is what stops a
vertical palette from narrowing its own container and then being unable to
discover it has room to go horizontal again.

Pass `horizontal` or `vertical` when you already know.
components.example:
<GraphCanvas
  onDrop={(point, event) => {
    const kind = readPaletteDrag(event);
    if (kind) addNode({ kind, position: point });
  }}
  overlay={
    <NodePalette
      items={[{ kind: 'task', label: 'Task' }, { kind: 'gate', label: 'Gate' }]}
      onSelect={(item) => addNodeAtCentre(item.kind)}
    />
  }
/>

props.name: items
props.description: The node types on offer.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible label for the group. Defaults to `"Node palette"`.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes merged onto the root element.

props.name: iconOnly
props.description:
Hide labels and show icons only. Useful for a narrow rail; items keep their
accessible name, so nothing is lost to a screen reader.

props.name: onDragStart
props.description: Called when a drag starts, if you want to show a drop hint.

props.name: onOrientationChange
props.description:
Called when `auto` settles on an axis, and whenever it changes. Useful for
adjusting surrounding layout to match.

props.name: onSelect
props.description:
Called when an item is activated by click or Enter, for creating without a
drag. Keyboard users need this — a drag-only palette is unreachable.

props.name: orientation
props.description:
Layout axis. Defaults to `"auto"`, which measures the available space and
picks whichever axis fits.

components.name: NumberField
components.description: A numeric property.

props.name: label
props.description: Label shown above the control.

props.name: value
props.description: Current value. `undefined` renders as empty.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes merged onto the field wrapper.

props.name: description
props.description: One line under the label explaining the property.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Render read-only.

props.name: error
props.description: Validation message, shown in the destructive colour.

props.name: max
props.description: Highest accepted value. Enforced by the browser, not by this component.

props.name: min
props.description: Lowest accepted value. Enforced by the browser, not by this component.

props.name: mixed
props.description:
Selected subjects hold different values. The control shows a placeholder
instead of a value, and editing applies to all of them.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the new value.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Hint shown in an empty control. Replaced by the mixed placeholder when `mixed`.

props.name: step
props.description: Increment for the spinner and arrow keys.

props.name: unit
props.description: Unit shown inside the control's trailing edge, e.g. `"px"`.

components.name: PaneHostProvider
components.description:
Declare that everything inside is hosted.

`SidebarPane` and the shell's tab factory do this for you. Wrap your own
container in it if you draw a title bar and want hosted components to defer.
components.example:
<PaneHostProvider chrome placement="bottom">
  <MyTitleBar />
  <ConnectedTerminalPane />
</PaneHostProvider>

props.name: children
props.description: Everything that should see this host.

props.name: chrome
props.description:
The host already draws a title bar and a close affordance, so a hosted
component should not draw its own.

props.name: placement
props.description: Where the host sits, when it knows. Useful for choosing a layout.

components.name: PropertyPanel
components.description:
An inspector: the properties of whatever is selected, as editable fields.

Give it the selection and a list of field descriptors. It reads each
property across every selected subject, renders the matching field, and hands
back new copies on edit — it holds no state and mutates nothing.

Three selection states are handled for you:

- **none** — the empty state.
- **one** — ordinary editing.
- **several** — shared values edit together; where subjects disagree the
  field shows *Mixed* rather than one subject's value, and editing applies to
  all of them.

That last case is the one hand-rolled inspectors usually skip, and skipping
it is how a multi-selection edit silently flattens data.

Every field is also exported on its own — reach for `TextField` and friends
when a property needs bespoke arrangement, and use `FieldShell` to make a
custom control look like the rest.
components.example:
<PropertyPanel
  subjects={selectedNodes}
  title={(nodes) => nodes.length > 1 ? `${nodes.length} nodes` : 'Node'}
  fields={[
    { key: 'data.label', label: 'Label' },
    { key: 'kind', label: 'Type', type: 'select',
      props: { options: [{ value: 'idea', label: 'Idea' }] } },
    { key: 'data.notes', label: 'Notes', type: 'textarea', group: 'Detail' },
    { key: 'data.tags', label: 'Tags', type: 'tags', group: 'Detail' },
  ]}
  onChange={(updated) => setNodes(merge(nodes, updated))}
/>

props.name: fields
props.description: The properties to show.

props.name: subjects
props.description:
The selected subjects. Zero renders the empty state, one edits normally,
several edit together with a mixed indicator where values differ.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible label for the region. Defaults to `"Properties"`.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes merged onto the root element.

props.name: emptyState
props.description: Shown when nothing is selected.

props.name: fieldTypes
props.description:
Field renderers by type. Defaults to {@link BUILT_IN_FIELD_TYPES}; spread
it to add your own without losing the built-ins.

props.name: groupOrder
props.description: Group headings render in this order. Unlisted groups follow, in first-seen order.

props.name: onChange
props.type: (updated: S[], field: IPropertyField<S>, value: unknown) => void
props.description:
Called with every subject updated. The panel produces new copies and never
mutates, so this is the whole edit — apply it to your state.

props.name: title
props.description:
Heading above the fields. Receives the selection, so it can read
"3 nodes selected" as easily as a name.

components.name: QuickSearch
components.description:
A compact search field with a grouped results dropdown, sized to sit inside a
{@link MenuBar}.

Presentational and fully controlled — it owns the query text, the open state
and the keyboard highlight, and nothing else. Searching is entirely yours:
results are pushed in via `results`, so the same component backs a local
array, a registry lookup, or a remote index.

Arrow keys move the highlight across groups, Enter selects, Escape closes.
components.example:
<QuickSearch
  results={hits}
  categories={['Actions', 'Files']}
  onQueryChange={setQuery}
  onSelect={(hit) => open(hit.id)}
/>

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Called when a row is clicked or chosen with Enter.

props.name: results
props.description:
Results for the current query. `QuickSearch` does no filtering — it renders
exactly what you give it, so you control matching, ranking and async
loading.

props.name: categories
props.description:
Explicit category order. Categories absent from this list are dropped, so
it doubles as a whitelist. Defaults to first-seen order.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes merged onto the root element.

props.name: debounceMs
props.description: Delay before `onQueryChange` fires, in ms. Defaults to `200`.

props.name: onQueryChange
props.description: Called on every keystroke, debounced by `debounceMs`.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder for the input. Defaults to `"Search…"`.

components.name: SearchWidget
components.description:
A full-height search panel: an input with autocomplete over a scrolling
result list. Sized for the sidebar, unlike the compact {@link QuickSearch}
that sits in the menu bar.

Controlled with respect to results — it owns the query text and debounces it
to `onSearch`, but never filters `results` itself. That keeps async and
remote search straightforward.
components.example:
<SearchWidget
  onSearch={setQuery}
  results={hits}
  loading={isFetching}
  suggestions={recentQueries}
  onSelect={(hit) => open(hit.id)}
/>

props.name: onSearch
props.description:
Called with the current query, debounced by 300ms. Do your matching here
and feed the outcome back through `results`.

props.name: onSelect
props.description: Called with the clicked result.

props.name: results
props.description: Results for the current query. The widget renders them as given.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes merged onto the root element.

props.name: loading
props.description: Swap the search icon for a spinner while a query is in flight.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Placeholder for the input. Defaults to `"Search..."`.

props.name: suggestions
props.description: Past or suggested queries offered as autocomplete below the input.

components.name: SelectField
components.description: A choice from a fixed set.

props.name: label
props.description: Label shown above the control.

props.name: options
props.description: The choices, in the order they should appear.

props.name: value
props.description: Current value. `undefined` renders as empty.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes merged onto the field wrapper.

props.name: description
props.description: One line under the label explaining the property.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Render read-only.

props.name: error
props.description: Validation message, shown in the destructive colour.

props.name: mixed
props.description:
Selected subjects hold different values. The control shows a placeholder
instead of a value, and editing applies to all of them.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the new value.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Shown as the first, unselected entry.

components.name: SettingsPanel
components.description:
Sidebar body for the Settings panel: a vertical list of theme choices.

Split out of {@link SidebarPane} so the pane stays a generic container. Pass
this (or your own component) as the sidebar's `children`.
components.example:
<SidebarPane title="Settings" onClose={close}>
  <SettingsPanel theme={theme} onThemeChange={setTheme} />
</SidebarPane>

props.name: onThemeChange
props.description: Called with the newly selected theme id.

props.name: theme
props.description: Currently selected theme id.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes merged onto the root element.

props.name: themes
props.description: Theme choices to offer. Defaults to every bundled theme.

components.name: ShellLayout
components.description:
The complete application shell: menu bar, activity bar, sidebar, a
`flexlayout-react` docking workspace, terminal, chat pane and status bar.

**This is where an application starts.** Call {@link initializeShell} once to
register your commands, menus and panels, render this component, and add
features by registering them rather than by restructuring the layout. Tab
contents resolve through the {@link componentRegistry}, so a new view is a
registration and a menu entry — the shell never needs to import it.

Configuration can arrive either way. Props are convenient for values that
change with your app's state; {@link initializeShell} is better for the fixed
set, since it runs once and works outside React. Props passed here are
written into the same stores on mount, so the two are interchangeable.

Internally this composes the `Connected*` component variants, which read from
the shell stores. Those components — and the pure ones beneath them — are
exported too, for the cases where you need to rearrange the frame itself.

Closing a tab marked dirty via `useLayoutStore().setTabDirty` prompts for
confirmation before the tab is removed.

props.name: centerMenuBarContent
props.description: Widget rendered between the menus and the right slot, sized for search.

props.name: disableLocalStorage
props.description:
Stop persisting the layout to `localStorage`. The workspace then resets to
`initialLayoutJson` on every load — useful for embedded or multi-tenant
shells where a per-browser layout would be wrong. Defaults to `false`.

props.name: initialLayoutJson
props.description:
Starting workspace, as a `flexlayout-react` JSON model. Applied once on
mount and only when nothing has been restored from storage, so it seeds a
first run without overwriting a layout the user has since arranged.

Ignored when `layoutModel` is provided, which takes control outright.

props.name: inspectorPanels
props.description:
Right-hand panels — inspectors, properties, anything about the current
selection rather than about navigation.

Registered exactly like `panels`, against a separate store, so the two
sides open and close independently: file tree on the left and properties on
the right, both at once. The right-hand rail appears only once at least one
is registered.

props.name: layoutModel
props.description:
Take control of the docking layout. When provided, the shell renders this
model and stops writing changes to `useLayoutStore` — useful for tests and
stories. Omit it to use the store's persisted model.

props.name: menuConfig
props.description: Menu structure, keyed by top-level menu name. Items dispatch by `commandId`.

props.name: onLayoutChange
props.description:
Called with the serialised model whenever the user moves, splits, opens or
closes a tab. Use it to persist the layout somewhere of your own — a user
profile on the server, say — instead of, or alongside, `localStorage`.

props.name: panels
props.description:
Sidebar panels to register. Each becomes an icon in the activity bar and
renders its `component` in the sidebar when selected.

props.name: rightMenuBarContent
props.description: Slot at the far right of the menu bar, for actions or a theme switcher.

props.name: slashCommands
props.description: Slash commands available in the chat pane.

props.name: statusBarConfig
props.description: Items for the status bar, grouped by their `alignment`.

props.name: title
props.description: Branding shown at the far left of the menu bar.

components.name: SidebarPane
components.description:
A docked side panel: a titled header with an optional close button, over a
scrolling body.

A pure container — it decides nothing about which panel is showing and holds
no state. Render whatever you like as `children`.

`side` docks it left (beside the {@link ActivityBar}) or right, where it
becomes an inspector. Both are the same component deliberately: before this
prop existed every application hand-rolled its own right-hand
`<div className="w-80 border-l …">`, and they all drifted apart.

For the store-backed variants used by `ShellLayout`, see
`ConnectedSidebarPane` and `ConnectedInspectorPane`.
components.example:
<SidebarPane title="Explorer" onClose={() => setActive(null)}>
  <TreeWidget data={files} />
</SidebarPane>

<SidebarPane title="Properties" side="right" width="320px">
  <PropertyPanel subjects={selected} fields={fields} />
</SidebarPane>

props.name: title
props.description:
Heading text. Rendered uppercase with letter-spacing; pass it in natural
case and let the component style it.

props.name: children
props.description: Panel body. Scrolls independently of the header.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes merged onto the root `<aside>`.

props.name: onClose
props.description:
Called when the close button is pressed. Omit it to hide the close button
entirely — useful when the pane is always visible.

props.name: side
props.description:
Which edge of the shell the pane is docked to. Defaults to `"left"`.

Only the divider moves — a right-hand pane is the same container, so an
inspector does not need a component of its own.

props.name: width
props.description: Fixed pane width, as a CSS length. Defaults to `"300px"`.

components.name: StaticField
components.description:
A read-only property: an id, a timestamp, a computed total.

Present because inspectors are full of values worth showing and not worth
editing, and a disabled text input reads as "you may not edit this yet"
rather than "this is derived".

props.name: mono
props.description: Render in a monospaced face — ids, hashes, coordinates.

components.name: StatusBar
components.description:
A VS Code-style status bar: a fixed-height footer with left, center and right
item groups. Items may be static labels or interactive buttons.

This component is fully controlled — it holds no state and reads no global
store. For the store-backed variant used by `ShellLayout`, see
{@link ConnectedStatusBar}.
components.example:
<StatusBar
  widgets={[
    { id: 'branch', label: 'main', icon: GitBranch, alignment: 'left', onClick: openBranches },
    { id: 'ln', label: 'Ln 12, Col 4', alignment: 'right' },
  ]}
/>

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible label for the landmark. Defaults to `"Status Bar"`.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes merged onto the root `<footer>`.

props.name: widgets
props.description:
Items to display. They are grouped by `alignment` and sorted by descending
`priority` within each group.

components.name: TagField
components.description:
A list-of-strings property.

Enter or the add button commits the draft; duplicates and blanks are
rejected silently rather than with an error, since neither is a mistake worth
interrupting for.

props.name: label
props.description: Label shown above the control.

props.name: value
props.description: Current value. `undefined` renders as empty.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes merged onto the field wrapper.

props.name: description
props.description: One line under the label explaining the property.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Render read-only.

props.name: error
props.description: Validation message, shown in the destructive colour.

props.name: mixed
props.description:
Selected subjects hold different values. The control shows a placeholder
instead of a value, and editing applies to all of them.

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the new value.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Hint shown in the draft box. Defaults to `"Add and press Enter"`.

props.name: suggestions
props.description: Offer these as a datalist while typing.

components.name: TerminalPane
components.description:
A terminal pane: a scrolling output log over a single-line input.

Presentational and fully controlled — it owns only the in-progress input
text. Visibility, history and command execution all belong to the caller.
For the store-backed variant with built-in `clear`/`help` handling, see
`ConnectedTerminalPane`.

**It fills whatever hosts it.** Bottom of the workspace, a side pane, or a
dockable tab — register it wherever it belongs. Inside a host that draws a
title bar it omits its own header and its own fixed height.

props.name: chrome
props.description:
Draw the title bar.

Left unset, this follows the host: inside a `SidebarPane` or a dockable tab
the title is already drawn, so the pane omits its own. Set it explicitly to
force either way.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes merged onto the root element.

props.name: height
props.description:
Height of the pane, as a CSS length.

Leave it unset inside a host that sizes its own children — a side pane or a
dockable tab — and the terminal fills the space instead. Defaults to
`"250px"` only when standalone.

props.name: history
props.description: Lines already written to the terminal, oldest first.

props.name: onClose
props.description: Called when the collapse or close button is pressed.

props.name: onCommand
props.description:
Called with the trimmed command text when the user presses Enter. Empty
input is swallowed and never reaches this handler.

The component does not echo the command or interpret it — append the echo
and any output to `history` yourself. This keeps command semantics
(`clear`, `help`, anything app-specific) entirely in your hands.

props.name: prompt
props.description: Prompt string shown before the input. Defaults to `"$"`.

props.name: title
props.description: Title shown in the pane header. Defaults to `"Terminal"`.

components.name: TextAreaField
components.description: A multi-line text property — notes, descriptions, evidence.

props.description: One line under the label explaining the property.

Selected subjects hold different values. The control shows a placeholder

props.name: description

props.name: inputType
props.description: Input type, for the browser's own affordances. Defaults to `"text"`.

props.name: mixed
props.description:
Selected subjects hold different values. The control shows a placeholder
instead of a value, and editing applies to all of them.

components.name: ThemeSwitcher
components.description:
A compact segmented control for switching themes.

Controlled — it renders `value` and reports changes through `onChange`, and
applies no classes to the document itself. For the store-backed variant that
also sets the theme class on `<html>`, see `ConnectedThemeSwitcher`.
components.example:
const [theme, setTheme] = useState('light');
<ThemeSwitcher value={theme} onChange={setTheme} />

props.name: onChange
props.description: Called with the newly selected theme id.

props.name: value
props.description: Currently selected theme id.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible label for the group. Defaults to `"Theme"`.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes merged onto the root element.

props.name: options
props.description:
Selectable themes. Defaults to every theme bundled in the library's
stylesheet. Supply your own to offer a different set.

components.name: TreeWidget
components.description:
A virtualised, domain-neutral tree with drag-to-move and a data-driven
right-click menu.

It renders any hierarchy — files, an org chart, a scene graph, nested
categories, an argument map. The component's only structural concept is
`isBranch`: branches expand and accept drops, leaves do neither. Everything
else — what a node *is*, what icon it carries, what actions it offers — is
yours to supply.

Rows are virtualised via `react-virtuoso`, so large trees stay responsive.

Controlled: expansion lives on your nodes as `isOpen` and changes are
reported through `onToggle`, so the tree never holds a second copy of your
data.

props.name: data
props.description: Root nodes. Expansion state lives on the nodes themselves via `isOpen`.

props.name: actions
props.description:
Entries for the right-click menu. Empty by default: the component ships no
actions of its own, because "New File" means nothing to an org chart.

With no entries, no menu appears.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Accessible label for the tree. Defaults to `"Tree"`.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes merged onto the root element.

props.name: indent
props.description: Indentation added per depth level, in px. Defaults to `12`.

props.name: onActivate
props.description: Called when a node is double-clicked or Enter is pressed on a leaf.

props.name: onMoveNode
props.description:
Called after a node is dragged onto a branch. Only branches accept drops.
Reparenting is yours to perform — the tree does not mutate `data`.

props.name: onToggle
props.description:
Called when a branch is clicked. Flip that node's `isOpen` in your own
state — the tree renders expansion but does not own it.

props.name: virtualized
props.description:
Virtualise rows with `react-virtuoso`. Leave on for large trees; turn it
off when every row must be present in the DOM — printing, full-text browser
search, or a test environment that can't measure layout. Defaults to `true`.

components.name: useGraphKeyboard
components.description:
Keyboard-driven graph navigation and editing.

Headless: it owns the focus, editing and connection cursors and reports what
should happen, but renders nothing and mutates nothing. That means it works
with `GraphNode` or with your own node rendering, and every mutation stays
subject to your validation and undo.

The default map, all overridable:

| Key | Action |
| :-- | :-- |
| Arrows | Move focus to the nearest node in that direction |
| Shift + Arrows | Nudge the focused node |
| Tab / Shift+Tab | Create a node connected to the focused one |
| Enter | Edit the focused node |
| `c` then a node | Connect from the focused node |
| Delete / Backspace | Delete the focused node |
| Escape | Leave edit mode, cancel a connection, or clear focus |

Arrow traversal is spatial rather than by insertion order — it picks the
nearest node in the direction travelled, penalising lateral offset, which is
what makes a hand-arranged diagram navigable without a mouse.

props.name: edges
props.description: The current edges. Used to reason about existing connections.

props.name: nodes
props.description: The current nodes. Traversal and placement are computed from these.

props.name: targetRef
props.description:
Element the listener attaches to. Bindings only fire while focus is inside
it, so several graphs can coexist on one page.

props.name: defaultFocusedId
props.description: Starting focus when uncontrolled.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Turn the whole thing off.

props.name: focusedId
props.description: Take control of which node has keyboard focus.

props.name: nudgeDistance
props.description: How far a nudge moves a node, in graph units. Defaults to `16`.

props.name: onConnect
props.description: Connect two nodes.

props.name: onCreateNode
props.type: (position: IPoint, context: { from?: string; direction?: Direction }) => string | undefined
props.description:
Create a node at a position, returning its id so focus can follow it. The
library never invents node content — you decide what a new node is.

props.name: onDeleteNode
props.description: Delete a node and its edges.

props.name: onEditNode
props.description: Enter edit mode for a node.

props.name: onFocusChange
props.description: Called whenever focus moves.

props.name: onMoveNode
props.description: Move a node, used by nudging.

components.name: useGraphLayout
components.description:
Apply a layout engine to a graph, with an escape hatch to hand placement.

Two kinds of mode:

- **An auto layout** — positions come from the engine. Your nodes' own
  positions are ignored while it is active, but never overwritten, so
  switching back to freeform restores the arrangement you had.
- **`freeform`** — positions are yours, exactly as stored.

Dragging a node under an auto layout escapes to freeform rather than fighting
the engine. That is the behaviour that makes auto layout usable: you can
always grab a node, and the graph stops rearranging itself the moment you do.

The hook derives positions and reports intent; it owns no node data and
mutates nothing.

props.name: edges
props.description: Your edges. Layouts that ignore structure ignore these.

props.name: nodes
props.description: Your nodes. Positions here are the hand-placed ones.

props.name: defaultMode
props.description: Starting mode when uncontrolled. Defaults to {@link FREEFORM}.

props.name: escapeOnDrag
props.description:
Dragging a node while an auto layout is active switches to freeform,
keeping the arrangement as it stood. Defaults to `true`.

Turn it off for a graph whose positions are entirely derived — a
visualisation rather than an editor — where a stray drag should be ignored.

props.name: layouts
props.description:
Named layouts to offer. Defaults to the bundled `vertical`, `horizontal`
and `grid`. Spread it to add your own.

props.name: mode
props.description: Take control of the mode.

props.name: onModeChange
props.description: Called whenever the mode changes, including the escape on drag.

props.name: onNodeMove
props.description:
Called when a node is moved by hand, so you can persist the position.

Without it, a drag under an auto layout still escapes to freeform but the
node snaps back to where it was — the engine no longer places it, and
nothing recorded where the pointer left it.

components.name: UserProfile
components.description:
An avatar and identity widget with a dropdown menu, sized for a menu bar's
right slot.

Fully controlled — it owns only its open/editing UI state. The identity comes
in as `profile`, edits go out through `onProfileChange`, and the menu is
whatever you pass as `actions`. It reads no store and prescribes no menu
items, so it works the same against a session hook, an auth provider, or
static props.
components.example:
<UserProfile
  profile={{ name: 'Ada Lovelace', role: 'Engineer', email: 'ada@example.com' }}
  onProfileChange={(next) => save(next)}
  actions={[
    { id: 'settings', label: 'Account Settings', icon: Settings, onSelect: openSettings },
    { id: 'out', label: 'Sign Out', icon: LogOut, onSelect: signOut, destructive: true, divider: true },
  ]}
/>

props.name: profile
props.description: The identity to display.

props.name: actions
props.description:
Actions listed in the dropdown. Empty by default — the component prescribes
no menu, since "Sign Out" and "Account Settings" mean different things in
every app.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes merged onto the trigger button.

props.name: onAvatarChange
props.description:
Called with a file the user picked for their avatar. Read it and update
`profile.avatarUrl` yourself — the component neither reads files nor holds
the result. Omit it to hide the upload affordance.

props.name: onClick
props.description:
Bypass the dropdown entirely and just report the click. Useful when the
profile should open a full settings tab instead of a menu.

props.name: onProfileChange
props.description:
Called with the new name and role when the inline editor is saved.
Omit it to hide the edit affordance entirely.

props.name: showName
props.description: Show the name and role beside the avatar. Defaults to `true`.
